# add-greeting: let alpha produce a greeting that beta prints

- size: project
- owner: demo-owner
- repos: [alpha, beta]
- supersedes: []
- approved: demo-owner 2026-10-01T09:00Z

## Why

Users of `beta` want a greeting on start-up, and the text belongs in `alpha`,
the shared library, so that other tools can use it too.

## Scope

In: the greeting text in `alpha`; printing it in `beta`.

Out: translations; any change to `gamma`.

## Requirements

### R1 Greeting text
`alpha` SHALL provide the greeting `hello, demo` for a caller that asks for it.

#### R1.S1 Default greeting
- GIVEN `alpha` at the branch head
- WHEN a caller asks for the greeting with no name
- THEN it gets the exact text `hello, demo` (11 characters, no trailing
  newline)

#### R1.S2 Name too long
- GIVEN a name of 65 characters
- WHEN a caller asks for the greeting with that name
- THEN it gets an error naming the 64-character limit, and no greeting

### R2 beta prints the greeting
`beta` SHALL print the greeting from `alpha` as its first line of output.

#### R2.S1 Start-up line
- GIVEN `beta` built against `alpha` at the branch head
- WHEN `beta` starts with no arguments
- THEN its first line of standard output is `hello, demo`, within 1 s of
  start (wall time)

## Approaches

1. Greeting in `alpha`, printed by `beta` (picked: one source of the text).
2. Greeting in `beta` only (rejected: other tools would copy the text).

## Open calls

1. The name limit is 64 characters, counted as Unicode code points.

# Plan: add-greeting

- change: add-greeting
- spec: changes/add-greeting/spec.md
- size: project

## 1. Goal and approach

`alpha` gains `greeting()`, which returns `hello, demo` and refuses a name
longer than 64 code points; `beta` prints that greeting as its first line of
output. Two build tasks, one per repo, with the project-level tests written in
parallel from the spec.

## 2. Interface contract

- alpha: `greeting(name: str | None = None) -> str`, in package `alpha`. With
  no name it returns `hello, demo`. With a name of at most 64 code points it
  returns `hello, <name>`. A longer name raises `ValueError`, whose message
  names the limit, 64.
- beta: `python3 -m beta`, with alpha importable, prints the greeting as its
  first line of standard output, then its existing banner `beta 1.0`.
- Project-level tests are Markdown files `test_R<n>_S<m>_<slug>.md` in
  `changes/add-greeting/tests/`, each with Given, When (one shell command, in
  which `$ALPHA` and `$BETA` are the alpha and beta checkouts of the commit
  set), Then and Fails if.
- Unit suites: `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` from the alpha root;
  `PYTHONPATH="$ALPHA" python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` from the beta
  root.

## 3. Global constraints

Verbatim from the spec:

- "it gets the exact text `hello, demo` (11 characters, no trailing
  newline)" (R1.S1)
- "within 1 s of start (wall time)" (R2.S1)
- "The name limit is 64 characters, counted as Unicode code points." (Open
  calls 1)

| Repo | File | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| alpha | `alpha/__init__.py` | `greeting()` |
| alpha | `tests/test_alpha.py` | unit tests of `greeting()` |
| beta | `beta/__main__.py` | print the greeting first |
| beta | `tests/test_beta.py` | unit test of the start-up output |
